steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Multiplication: (AB)_{ij} = Σₖ A_{ik}B_{kj} -- non-commutative, associative, distributive

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: det 2x2: |a b; c d| = ad - bc; det 3x3: cofactor expansion or Sarrus

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Inverse 2x2: A⁻¹ = (1/det)[d -b; -c a]; 3x3: adj(A)/det(A) via minors/cofactors

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: System AX = B: if det(A) != 0, X = A⁻¹B (unique solution); if det(A) = 0, either no solution or infinite

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [3 2; 1 4]. Diagonalise A --- Solution: det(A-λI) = (3-λ)(4-λ)-2 = λ^2-7λ+10 = (λ-5)(λ-2)=0 -> λ=5,2. λ=5: [−2 2; 1 −1]v=0 -> v₁=[1;1]. λ=2: [1 2; 1 2]v=0 -> v₂=[2;−1]. P=[1 2; 1 −1], D=[5 0; 0 2]. Check P⁻¹AP=D

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Find det and inverse of [2 1 3; 0 1 4; 5 6 0] | Solve using matrix inverse: 2x+y-z=1, x+2y+z=2, 3x-y+2z=3 | Find matrix for rotation by 90 deg about origin followed by reflection in y=x

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of matrices with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [3 2; 1 4]. Diagonalise A. Solution: det(A-λI) = (3-λ)(4-λ)-2 = λ^2-7λ+10 = (λ-5)(λ-2)=0 -> λ=5,2. λ=5: [−2 2; 1 −1]v=0 -> v₁=[1;1]. λ=2: [1 2; 1 2]v=0 -> v₂=[2;−1]. P=[1 2; 1 −1], D=[5 0; 0 2]. Check P⁻¹AP=D Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.

steps.title: Homework
steps.body: Find det and inverse of [2 1 3; 0 1 4; 5 6 0] Solve using matrix inverse: 2x+y-z=1, x+2y+z=2, 3x-y+2z=3 Find matrix for rotation by 90 deg about origin followed by reflection in y=x Find eigenvalues of [4 1; 2 3] and corresponding eigenvectors Show [1 2; 2 1] is diagonalisable
